title: TEMPELHOF · 1948 — DIE WINDPILGER
brief:
USER'S CHOICE: Tempelhof B's wind, airplanes, kites and cargo-pilgrims, but MUCH MORE FRIGHTENING, occult, elaborate and fantastical; much less zombie and less machinery. Keep the 1948 airlift anchors: recognisable long curved limestone airport terminal, huge hangar, Feld grass/runways and C-47/Rosinenbomber twin-engine cargo aircraft. Planes are spectral relics worshipped by a fictional WIND CULT, not a modern military faction. Ink navy/charcoal, cold fog ivory, bruised violet, deep crimson, oxidised silver and eerie pale mint witchlight. No yellow paint, no brass gadget aesthetic. Human cultists are alive, fully clothed masked ritualists, not rotting skeletal ghouls.
KEY SCENE: a violent crosswind bends grass and drives immense torn red/ivory parachute banners; one abandoned unbranded silver/grey aircraft is a ritual shrine, ghost cargo planes bank through a black storm eclipse, streams of souls and vapor trace wing-shaped spirals. Cold mint St Elmo fire runs down guy ropes and along wings, violet sheet lightning silhouettes giant hanging sailcloth effigies; small blood-red votive lamps anchor ritual circles on cracked wet runway. Distinct light sources and volumetric rays, beautiful frightening readable silhouettes, not simple orange sunset.
ARCHITECTURE VIGNETTES: (1) eroded curved Flughafen terminal with wind-torn pilgrimage drapery; (2) dark Hangar der Letzten Landung, converted to a fabric/rope cathedral with suspended ghost-wing altar; (3) runway wind shrine built from an aircraft nose, field stones, cargo net and taut vast ritual kites. Magic and terrifying cloth mass, NOT a robot, no engine-armour torso, no fuel tanks, no gears, no exposed zombie rib cage. Include him distant in the scene and as separate full-body boss concept.
EMBLEMATIC SET: ORNAT DES GEGENWINDS, lavish layered ink-indigo and ivory storm robes, sculpted kite-frame shoulder mantle, huge split parachute cape with crimson rope embroidery, wind-bell charms, hand-bound quilted gauntlets and heavy boots, carved ivory aviator ritual mask tilted to side so survivor's face remains visible. Back view shows a spectacular ritual wing-pattern cape held by tether knots, front view carries red scarf. Actual complete fantasy ARPG outfit, not generic flight-jacket starter gear.
